# `kernel/schema/BinaryPack.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/schema/BinaryPack.js`

BinaryPack.js — custom binary codec, zero external dependencies. Wire format: MessagePack specification (https://msgpack.org/index.html) Implemented from spec only — not copied from any library. API: pack(value)         → Uint8Array unpack(buf)         → value packToBase64(value) → string  (base64-encoded packed bytes) unpackBase64(str)   → value Supported types: null / undefined → nil boolean          → true / false integer (safe)   → positive/negative fixint, uint8-32, int8-32 float            → float64 string           → fixstr / str8 / str16 / str32 Uint8Array       → bin8 / bin16 / bin32 Array            → fixarray / array16 / array32 Object (plain)   → fixmap / map16 / map32 Byte layout (big-endian throughout, per spec): 0x00–0x7f  positive fixint 0x80–0x8f  fixmap   (N = low nibble) 0x90–0x9f  fixarray (N = low nibble) 0xa0–0xbf  fixstr   (N = low 5 bits) 0xc0       nil 0xc2       false 0xc3       true 0xc4–0xc6  bin8 / bin16 / bin32 0xca       float32   (encode uses float64 for precision) 0xcb       float64 0xcc–0xcf  uint8 / uint16 / uint32 / uint64* 0xd0–0xd3  int8  / int16  / int32  / int64* 0xd9–0xdb  str8  / str16  / str32 0xdc–0xdd  array16 / array32 0xde–0xdf  map16   / map32 0xe0–0xff  negative fixint * int64/uint64 are encoded as float64 when |v| > 2^32 (JS safe integer limit).

## Functions

### `pack(value)`

Encode any JS value to a Uint8Array (MessagePack wire format).

### `unpack(buf)`

Decode a Uint8Array or ArrayBuffer from MessagePack wire format.

### `packToBase64(value)`

Pack and base64-encode — useful for JSON embedding and localStorage.

### `unpackBase64(str)`

Decode a base64-encoded pack string.

### `packedSize(value)`

Return the packed byte-size of a value without keeping the buffer.

### `packEqual(a, b)`

Compare two values by structural equality using pack → byte comparison.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
